original_test_intent: Verify that the BMC reaches the USB hub physically located on the intended HPM and, as the Procedure states, that the complete HPM downstream-device population enumerates at the expected ports and speeds.
original_method: Identify HPM slot/PN/revision and population, bind the BMC USB controller/root port through board connector and cable to that HPM hub, specify the native or proxy enumeration surface, hub identity and every expected child; have an operator confirm/photograph the HPM path; capture the full USB tree and descriptors without filtering; compare port number, VID:PID/product/serial, class and negotiated speed for hub and children; preserve reset/flap/error and BMC/HPM health evidence, with no unapproved replug, reset, rebind or power operation.
manual_activity: An operator proves which HPM is populated, inspects/photographs the BMC-to-HPM hub cable and connectors, and confirms the path remains untouched while read-only topology is captured.
required_inputs: Target HPM slot/PN/revision/population and BMC controller/root-port/connector/cable/hub topology
Expected HPM hub and per-port downstream device identity/speed manifest
Decision on hub-only versus all-downstream acceptance, error tolerance, physical procedure and recovery
safety_requirements: Bind all evidence to the selected HPM instance and exact root-port/port chain
Collect read-only complete topology/descriptors; do not infer identity from the generic word `hub`
Do not unplug/replug HPM USB, reset/deauthorize devices, unbind/rebind drivers, change authorization or power-cycle the HPM
Preserve USB/BMC/HPM errors and management state; do not clear evidence
Stop on wrong HPM, reset storm, device flapping, link downgrade or management instability; no automatic retry
agent_execution_scope: Verify HPM identity/population, physical/logical path, enumeration owner and expected hub/child oracle
After operator confirmation, collect full tree/descriptors and timestamped USB/BMC/HPM health/error evidence
Compare every expected port/device and negotiated speed, recording missing, unexpected, moved or downgraded entries
Do not accept any generic hub, use insecure/truncated commands, change USB/HPM state or issue the DUT verdict
engineer_actions: Resolve whether Criteria should require only the HPM hub or also all downstream devices named by Procedure
Approve HPM identity/population, BMC-to-HPM USB topology, enumeration surface and complete per-port device/speed manifest
Review physical and HPM-bound topology evidence and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: An unfiltered `lsusb -t` plus full descriptors can support the software portion only on the authoritative surface. The proposed password-exposing SSH, host-key bypass, `grep` and `head` lose identity and completeness.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: On the approved enumeration endpoint, capture complete USB topology and descriptors for the exact BMC root-port-to-HPM route, plus full kernel/reset history, after the operator verifies HPM physical population.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: BMC-to-HPM USB hub scope, AI_VR_USB_BMC_to_HPM bundle and 20/20-minute allocation remain; HPM instance and acceptance oracle are not inferred.

modernized_recommendation.status: LOW READ-ONLY HPM-BOUND USB HUB AND DOWNSTREAM TOPOLOGY CHECK
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Correlate the populated HPM's connector chain with an exact USB port tree and validate the hub plus every required child and speed against a revision-controlled manifest.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds HPM instance/population identity, per-port children, link speed, complete error evidence and explicit acceptance-scope handling.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Another platform hub can satisfy the hub-only string check, and the intended HPM hub can enumerate while individual downstream HPM functions remain absent or at the wrong port/speed.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: The HPM path may carry management-critical peripherals; reset, rebind or service actions can disrupt more than the hub being reviewed.

project_override_considerations: If the selected HPM is absent by approved configuration, record the population state and apply the engineer-approved N/A policy rather than substituting another HPM or hub. Host enumeration is acceptable only with documented proxy mapping.
expected_evidence: Exact row/variant/hash, authorization, resolved acceptance scope and target HPM slot/PN/revision/population
Complete authoritative USB tree and descriptors binding exact hub and every expected per-port child with speeds
Frozen downstream manifest comparison including absent, unexpected, moved or downgraded devices
Pre/post USB reset/flap/error evidence and stable BMC/HPM state
Conflict disposition, discrepancy/recovery record and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The Procedure requires all downstream devices to be shown, but the Criteria defines PASS from hub detection alone. The latter can pass an incompletely populated or nonfunctional HPM tree.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The BMC-to-HPM topology review is understandable and evidence for both scopes can be collected. Engineer acceptance is pending but static review can continue.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Functionality row 2170 Wistron-GB NV PVP HW-00057-V002: decide hub-only versus exact hub plus all downstream acceptance; approve target HPM slot/PN/revision/population, BMC controller/root-port/connector/cable-to-HPM-hub mapping, enumeration surface, per-port VID:PID/product/serial/class/speed manifest, N/A policy, error limits, aborts, and recovery.

review_improvement: Makes the HPM instance and each required child explicit and preserves the Master acceptance conflict, preventing another hub or an empty HPM hub from producing a false pass.
independent_technical_reasoning: This row differs from the preceding HMC case because the target is a potentially replaceable/population-dependent HPM. Evidence must bind the selected HPM slot and board identity, not merely a USB hub. Since a hub can enumerate with dead or absent child functions, Procedure coverage materially exceeds the Criteria. The correct static review retains both requirements, records the conflict, and requires a per-port manifest rather than silently reducing the case to hub presence.
